<reason>A very tight, high-quality debate. PRO built a vivid, motion-aligned case (the silent exit, redistribution of expression, "CON concedes the principle and only argues about the instrument") and its closing weighing on whose risk the platform carries was strong. But CON's scale-to-automation reframe survived the whole exchange: when PRO answered CON's funding question with severity triage, CON turned that into a mapped concession — humans on already-enforced severe cases, machines on the ambiguous middle where every false positive and the mass-reported girl herself live. CON also answered both pressure questions crisply (doxxing already at max severity, friction beats throwaways; the "too weak/too strong" contradiction resolved into the regressive-asymmetry thesis), while PRO's answer to "what does the motion add over design" was thinner and its "normative not invoice" move was fairly met. CON's "setting isn't a verdict" distinction is contestable and CON paid execution costs (three clipped turns, a misreference), which keeps the margin thin, but CON made the marginal product of the motion the decisive question and won it more cleanly.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B4.5–B4.6: CON took PRO's own triage answer ("cheap, reversible responses" for the low-grade mass) and showed it hands exactly the ambiguous middle to automation — "PRO's triage doesn't answer my case; it maps it" — which PRO's closing never directly dislodged.</best_rebuttal>
